newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Comalco, Chevron said to agree jv projects.
newsitem.headline: Comalco, Chevron said to agree jv projects.

text.p: Aluminium producer Comalco Ltd and U.S. oil major Chevron Corp have agreed to pursue possible joint development of A$4 billion worth of projects in Queensland, The Australian Financial Review reported on Thursday.
The newspaper said the projects would involve Comalco's proposed alumina refinery and Chevron's proposed gas pipeline between Papua New Guinea and Australia.
"The agreement, which may be signed next week, will be non-binding," the newspaper said.
"But it will be designed to cement a future for both projects," it said.
The federal and Queensland state governments were expected to support the agreement, it said.

Comalco is considering several sites for a A$1 billion alumina refinery which would process bauxite from the Weipa mine while Chevron is studying the feasibility of building a pipeline to carry gas from the Kutubu project to northern Queensland. The value of the gas project has been put at about A$3 billion.
"It is no secret we have been talking a lot with Comalco," the newspaper quoted a pipeline project source as saying.
The deal between the companies would be designed solely to investigate potential benefits to each project, it said.
Comalco is 67 percent owned by Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd.
